# package tracetest

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-modbus-trace/trace/tracetest"
```

Package tracetest builds synthetic packet traces with a known ground truth, for the tests of this module and of the applications built on it.

A Builder writes a classic pcap or pcapng stream (optionally gzip) as it goes, so a trace of any size can be produced without being held in memory. Connections are scripted: each Write sends Modbus ADUs (or raw bytes) in one direction, segmented by a policy and with optional faults (loss, retransmission, conflicting overlap, reordering, duplicates on a second interface, snap-length truncation, IP fragmentation). Every ADU written is recorded in the Truth with its fate, and the TCP conditions a correct reassembler must report are counted there too.

```go
type ADU struct {
	Conn      uint32 // connection number, in order of the first packet (1-based)
	Dir       Dir
	TID       uint16
	Unit      uint8
	PDU       []byte
	Lost      bool // some of its bytes were never captured
	Truncated bool // the snap length cut it; the visible bytes are there
	Resynced  bool // the first ADU after a gap in its direction
}
```

### type Conn

```go
type Conn struct {

	// bytes lost since the last captured data; -1: none
	// the direction has captured data
	// A hole stays open (for a reader that declares a loss only once the
	// peer acknowledged past it and later data waits behind it) until both
	// happened.

	// the next delivered ADU follows a gap
	// the direction's last write, for Resend

}
```

Conn is a scripted TCP connection.

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (c *Conn) Close()
```

Close ends the connection with FIN in both directions.

#### func (Conn) ID

```go
func (c *Conn) ID() uint32
```

ID returns the connection number (0 before its first packet).

#### func (Conn) Keepalive

```go
func (c *Conn) Keepalive(d Dir)
```

Keepalive writes a keepalive probe (one old byte) in direction d. It is skipped where it would be ambiguous: before the direction sent captured data (it would start the stream) and after an unresolved loss (its byte would fill the hole).

#### func (Conn) Request

```go
func (c *Conn) Request(tid uint16, unit uint8, pdu []byte)
```

Request writes one request ADU to the server.

#### func (Conn) Resend

```go
func (c *Conn) Resend(d Dir)
```

Resend sends the direction's last Write again as one identical segment, at this point of the trace, which WriteOpts.Retransmit cannot do. The write must have been captured whole and be longer than one byte (see Keepalive).

#### func (Conn) Reset

```go
func (c *Conn) Reset(d Dir)
```

Reset ends the connection with an RST from d.

#### func (Conn) Response

```go
func (c *Conn) Response(tid uint16, unit uint8, pdu []byte)
```

Response writes one response ADU to the client.


Write sends frames back to back as one write in direction d.

### type Link

```go
type Link int
```

Link is the link-layer framing of an interface.

```go
const (
	Ethernet     Link = iota // Ethernet II
	EthernetVLAN             // Ethernet with one 802.1Q tag
	EthernetQinQ             // Ethernet with an 802.1ad and an 802.1Q tag
	Null                     // BSD loopback (link type 0, family in little endian)
	Loop                     // OpenBSD loopback (link type 108, family in big endian)
	Raw                      // raw IP (link type 101)
	IPv4Link                 // link type 228
	IPv6Link                 // link type 229
	SLL                      // Linux cooked v1 (113)
	SLL2                     // Linux cooked v2 (276)
)
```

### type Truth

```go
type Truth struct {
	Packets     uint64 // packet records written
	Conns       uint32 // connections (epochs) that sent a packet
	Midstream   uint64 // connections without a captured handshake
	ADUs        []ADU
	Gaps        uint64 // holes in a direction's byte stream
	GapBytes    uint64
	Retransmits uint64 // segments that carry only bytes already seen
	Conflicts   uint64 // ... whose bytes differ from the first copy
	OutOfOrder  uint64 // segments that arrived before a gap before them was filled
	Keepalives  uint64
}
```

Truth is what a correct reader, reassembler and framer must report.

### type WriteOpts

```go
type WriteOpts struct {
	Seg        []int // segment sizes; the rest goes in MSS-sized segments
	OneByte    bool  // one byte per segment
	Lose       []int // segment indices never captured
	Retransmit []int // indices sent again, identical, after the write
	Conflict   []int // indices sent again with the last byte changed
	Duplicate  []int // indices captured a second time on DupIface
	DupIface   int
	Reverse    bool // segments in reverse order
	Fragment   int  // IP fragments of this payload size (a multiple of 8)
	Snap       int  // capture only the first Snap payload bytes of each segment
}
```

WriteOpts shape one Write.
